name: gb_status
description: What Greenbox is showing now: open 3D tab, loaded model, rig step, joints, vehicle parts, play test / mocap state.

name: gb_screenshot
description: Picture of the 3D view of a Greenbox page (default: the open one). Use it to check your work.

page.description: create | vehicle | playtest | mocap | retarget (default: current)

name: gb_open
description: Open a Greenbox 3D tab. Tabs stay alive, so work in other tabs is kept.

name: gb_click
description: Click a button/element in a Greenbox page (CSS selector, or visible text with "text=...").

name: gb_set_value
description: Set an input/select value in a Greenbox page and fire its change event.

name: gb_run_js
description: Run JavaScript inside a Greenbox page (async function body; `return` a JSON value). Globals: create page `__gb3d` (Mesh2Motion engine: load_model_step, edit_skeleton_step, easy_rig, weight_skin_step, animations_listing_step, quick_export_all(fmt)), vehicle `__vehicle` (wheels, mechs, new_mech(kind), build_rig(), clips, play(i)), playtest `__playtest` (ctrl), mocap `__mocap`. THREE objects are live.

name: gb_rig_auto
description: On the "Use your model" tab: scan the loaded model and place every joint of the human skeleton (load the human skeleton first if needed).

name: gb_joints_get
description: World positions of every joint on the "Use your model" tab (editing step).

name: gb_joints_set
description: Move joints to world positions {name: [x,y,z]} on the "Use your model" tab (children follow unless listed).

name: gb_rig_finish
description: On "Use your model": compute skin weights and go to the animation list (178 animations).

name: gb_export
description: Export from a Greenbox page: create = rigged model + all animations, vehicle = vehicle rig, mocap = clip. Returns the file (base64) to the caller, which can save it.

name: gb_load_file
description: Load a 3D model / video file into a Greenbox page. `data_b64` is the file content (the MCP server fills it from a path on disk).

name: gb_analyze
description: Analyse the model loaded on a page: what it is (humanoid / quadruped / vehicle / object) and its anchor points — head, arms, legs and accessories (tail, wings, ears, horns, hair, cape, held items) with joint positions inside the mesh. On "vehicle" it can also create a bone chain on every branch (make_bones).

make_bones.description: vehicle page: create free bones along every branch (default true)

name: gb_smash
description: SMASH DOWN blockout (a shooting ad: a wall of cans / boxes on a table, a gun in the middle). Actions: status (ammo, knocked, blocks, layout), preset {name: wall | pyramid | towers | checker | random}, reset (rebuild the stack), shoot {x, y} (0..1 of the 9:16 view), auto {on} (auto shoot), record (start recording the 9:16 view), stop (stop and save the blockout video), prompt (the Seedance video-to-video prompt for the chosen theme), base {name: table | pedestal | steps | float | spin (turntable) | slide (moves side to side), speed? 0–3, color? "#rrggbb"} (what the stack stands on), hit {mode: knock | break} (a hit knocks pieces over, or breaks them into bits), build_base {shape?: box | round, thick? m (0.02–0.8), width? ×(0.5–2.2), depth? ×(0.5–4), legs?: pole | two | four | solid | none} (your own base).

name: gb_vehicle
description: Vehicles / any-model rig tab. Actions: auto_rig (one click: what was learned from 4–5 ★ rigs of the same shape + shape scan + bones + all keyframed animations), rate {score 1–5} (rate the rig on screen; 4–5 ★ rigs teach the next auto_rig), scan_wheels, find_tracks (caterpillar belts as bone chains), add_bone {name, at:[x,y,z], parent?, axis?} (a free bone with its joint at a point; parent chains it), assign_box {part, min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z]} (give every vertex inside a box to a part / bone), separate {part} (cut the part into its own mesh and fill the holes), set_type {type: car|truck|tracked|roller}, build (rig + animations), play {clip}, stop, list.

name: gb_map
description: Play-test map editor (terrain + objects, RTS-style). Actions: preset {preset: flat|hills|island|valley|mountains}, add {object: pine|tree|bush|rock|house|tower|wall|fence|hwall|door|window|crate|barrel|flag|roof|floor|stairs, x, z, rot?, scale?, level?} (level: storey 0..4, 2.8 m each; hwall / door / window: one 3 m house-wall piece centred at x, z, rot 0 = along X, pi/2 = along Z, ends on grid points every 1.5 m; roof: x, z = a point inside closed walls on that level, the roof fits the room; floor: x, z inside a closed room, level 0 = wooden floor, level 1+ = slab over the walls of level-1 with holes over stairs; stairs: 1.5 x 4.5 m from level to level+1, rot in 90 degree steps, rising towards +z when rot 0), sculpt {tool: raise|lower|flatten|smooth|paint, x, z, radius?, strength?, ground?: 0 grass 1 dirt 2 sand 3 rock 4 snow 5 road 6 water bed}, water {level}, export_blender (Python script that rebuilds the map in Blender), export_glb, get (map JSON summary). Also: dig {x, z, radius?, depth?} carves a flat-bottomed hole; pour {x, z, fill?: 0.3..1} fills the hole / channel at (x, z) with water up to its rim; sea {on: bool}; erase {x, z, radius?} removes props there; shot_add {mode?: fixed|look|follow, follow?: "player"|object name, t?, dur?, fov?} saves the current camera view as a shot; shots (list); shots_play; layout {image_b64, legend?: [{color:"#rrggbb", kind}]} builds the map from a top-down colour plan (kinds: background grass water sand road dirt mountain snow forest tree house tower wall fence rock flag); export_unity (C# script that plays the shots); export_playable {cta?: store / landing link, title?: game name on the loading screen + end card, limit?: seconds of play before the end card (0 = when every upgrade is bought)} = the playable ad as one HTML file (map + the Play test player + the 2D plan gameplay; build the plan first); plan {plan: {shapes: [{id, kind: zone|block|source|machine|stack|counter|unlock|player, form: rect|ellipse, x, z, w, d, r, label, color, height, gives?, takes?, time?, price?, model?}], wires: [{id, from, to, mode: carry|belt|unlock}]}, play?: bool} builds a 2D plan as a 3D playable (and plays it); clear (empty map).

name: gb_hpbar
description: HP-bar / HUD video layer (its own page, exported separately: green MP4 for Keylight or alpha .MOV). Actions: get, set {settings: partial state, e.g. {hero:{name,level}, hp:{max,start}, mp:{on,max}, dur, fps, size:"1080x1920", bg:"green"|"black"|"clear"}}, events {events:[{t: seconds, kind: dmg|heal|set|mana-|mana+, v: amount}]} (replaces the list: when the hero is hit), export_mov, export_mp4 (run in the background: then call export_status every ~5 s until state is "done"; it gives the saved file path under Greenbox/exports/hud), export_status. Boss bar: set {settings:{boss:{on:true, name, max, start, layers, w, h, x, y}}} and events with who:"boss". Hero bar size: hp:{w, h, round, drain, hold}, hud:{flip, on, x, y}. Countdown: page {page:"count"} then set {settings:{cd:{from, to, start, format: s|mmss|dec|dec2, size, x, y, color, stroke, sw, ring, end, endHold, warn}}} and export like the HP bar.

name: gb_drive
description: Driving overlay (Lái xe → Vô lăng & bàn đạp): steering wheel + 2 pedals, or the excavator kit: ONE joystick lever (slot lever: A/D tilts it, W pushes, S pulls) + a W A S D key cluster that lights up (slot keys) + a console picture (slot dash). Actions: layout (a picture of the layout + positions: SHOW IT TO THE USER and agree the changes first), set_layout {items, confirmed: true} (only after the user said OK; ids dash|pad|lever|keys|wheel|brake|gas|gear|speedo, hidden:true/false switches a part off/on), image {slot: dash|pad|lever|wheel|brake|gas, path | url} (a picture for that part, PNG with transparent background is best), status, load {path} (the video), auto (the AI reads the video: scenery sliding sideways = steering, how fast the picture changes = gas / brake; makes the take), export {mode: "mov" = transparent .MOV (RGB + alpha, PNG frames) of the overlay only, for After Effects / Premiere; "green" / "black" = keyed backgrounds; "video" = finished MP4 with the gameplay}. Export runs in the background: call status until state is "done" (it gives the saved file path) or "error".

path.description: load: the video file on this computer; image: the picture file

url.description: image / load: a link to the picture or video (Higgsfield result…); it is downloaded on this computer

items.description: set_layout: [{id: dash|pad|lever|keys|wheel|brake|gas|gear|speedo, x?, y?, size?, w?, rot?, hidden?}] in frame pixels

confirmed.description: set_layout: true only after the user saw the layout picture and said OK to these changes

name: gb_sfx
description: SFX sync (Post → Gắn SFX): put sounds on the hits of a finished video. Actions: status (sounds in the library, cues found, clips placed), load {video_b64, name} (MCP: {path}), analyze (finds the hits / cue points), add_all {sound: name or part of it, e.g. "coin"} (that sound on EVERY cue, aligned by its loudest point; repeat with other sounds), export (renders the MP4 with sound). Built-in sounds: Impact boom, Rock crunch, Coin ding, Sparkle shimmer, Whoosh, Upgrade rise, Water splash; the user can add their own in the page.

name: gb_to_playtest
description: Send the character rigged on "Use your model" (after gb_rig_finish) to Play test with its animations, like the "🎮 Play test this character" button. Waits until it is the player.

name: gb_recipe
description: Step-by-step recipe to make a playable ad from a 3D model with the Greenbox tools (rig → Play test → map → 2D plan gameplay → test → HTML export). Read it before starting such a job.

name: gb_drama
description:
AI Drama (script → characters → clips → episode). AI Drama in Greenbox (Cockpit group 🎬 AI Drama, page drama.html). The user works there; every button that needs you posts a request into the Greenbox chat: "[AI Drama #N] kind: …". Loop: gb_inbox {wait: 50} → for each [AI Drama #N] request: gb_drama {action: "get"} (settings, script, characters, open requests) → do it → gb_drama {action: "done", id: N}. The page updates live while you work (the user watches), so narrate with gb_drama {action: "say", text}.
Kinds: write_script = write the full script from settings.text in Vietnamese (or the story's language): gb_drama {action: "script", script: {title, logline, chars: [{name, role, look}], eps: [{title, summary, beats: [{scene, chars: [names], action, lines: [{who, text}], sec, prompt}]}]}}. Single film (settings.type "single") = ONE entry in eps whose beats are the film's beats; series = settings.eps_n episodes of about settings.ep_sec seconds each. LONG (settings.long, more than 5 min per film / episode, up to 1 hour): give each episode segs = settings.parts_per_episode parts [{title, summary, sec ≈ settings.part_sec}] and write beats (with seg: 0) ONLY for part 1 — never the whole hour at once. write_beats {ep, seg} = write that part's beats: gb_drama {action: "beats", ep, seg, beats: [...]} (about part_sec / clip beats). gen_segment {ep, seg} = make the clips of that part only (like gen_episode). Every beat lasts settings.clip seconds (5 / 10 / 15 = one Higgsfield clip); the beats' sec must add up to the episode / film length. look = an English picture prompt in settings.style + settings.country; prompt = an English image-to-video prompt (camera, action, mood, style, aspect settings.ratio), naming the characters. rewrite_episode {ep} = rewrite that episode only (gb_drama {action: "script", ep, script: {summary, beats}}). char_image {name | names} = make the character picture(s) on Higgsfield (higgsfield.ai, in the browser; the user must be signed in — never sign in for them): portrait / character sheet from the character's look, settings.style, plain background; then gb_drama {action: "char", name, url} with the picture's link (the result image src or its download link — Greenbox downloads it on this computer; or path = a file already on this computer); you may also pass new_name / look. gen_episode {ep} / gen_beat {ep, beat} = image-to-video on Higgsfield, one clip per beat (the beat prompt + the pictures of the characters in it, duration = beat sec, aspect settings.ratio): before each batch ask the user to approve the credits with gb_say + gb_inbox (e.g. "8 clips × 10 s, OK?"); mark each beat with gb_drama {action: "beat", ep, beat, status: "gen"} while it renders, then gb_drama {action: "clip", ep, beat, url} (the video src / download link; or path). Only what was asked: one episode (series) or one beat (single film) at a time. name_hooks {eps} = gb_drama {action: "episode", ep, title, hook} for those episodes (hook = the first 3 seconds that make people stay). merge {ep} = gb_drama {action: "merge", ep} joins that episode's clips in order with ffmpeg on this computer and puts the MP4 back on the page. HIGGSFIELD: prefer the Higgsfield MCP tools (connector https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp) — generate there and pass the result link with url; only without them use higgsfield.ai in the browser. settings.unlimited (default true) = use Higgsfield's Unlimited mode / unlimited models so no credits are spent; when it is false ask before spending credits. Per-beat buttons (Production): prompt_beat {ep, beat, idea} = from the beat (action, lines, characters' looks, style) and the user's idea write an English picture prompt and an image-to-video prompt: gb_drama {action: "prompts", ep, beat, img_prompt, prompt}. gen_image {ep, beat} = make the scene picture from img_prompt (use the characters' pictures as references when the tool takes them), aspect settings.ratio: gb_drama {action: "beat", ep, beat, status: "img"} while it renders, then gb_drama {action: "still", ep, beat, url}. gen_beat {ep, beat} = image-to-video from the beat's still (or the character pictures) + prompt, duration = beat sec: gb_drama {action: "clip", ep, beat, url}. STUDIO (DramaClaw-style parts): extract_assets {kind: scenes|props} = read the script and add every scene / prop: gb_drama {action: "asset", kind: "scene"|"prop", name, look} (look = English picture prompt). asset_image {kind, name | names} = make the picture on Higgsfield (wide 16:9 for scenes, plain background for props), then gb_drama {action: "asset", kind, name, url}. voice_sample {name} ("__narrator" = narrator) = a short voice sample from the voice desc (Higgsfield / any TTS you have): gb_drama {action: "voice", name, url | path, desc?}. voice {ep, beat} / voice_episode {ep} = voice-over of the beat lines in each character's voice: gb_drama {action: "voice", ep, beat, url | path}. music {ep} = background music for the episode: gb_drama {action: "music", ep, url | path}. storyboard {ep} = the first-frame picture of every beat of that episode (like gen_image for each). style_extract = look at the reference (gb_drama {action: "media_out", what: "style"} saves it as a file) and write the style: gb_drama {action: "style", name, prompt}. Always add settings/style.prompt to every picture / video prompt. fix_qc {ep, issues} = the page's QC found problems in that episode (get → qc lists them: dialogue too long for the clip, total length off, missing prompt, unknown character): rewrite it so they are gone, same plot and beat count: gb_drama {action: "script", ep, script: {summary, beats}}. QUALITY for every script: each episode opens with a hook inside the first 3 seconds and ends on a cliffhanger; one beat = one shot = one place + one clear action; at most 3 spoken words per second of the beat; prompt order = shot size + camera move, who (name + 3-word look) does what, place, light, mood, style, aspect. Requests the user's own API key already answers (⚡ in the log) never reach you. director {text} = Xia Director chat: answer the user (and edit the project with the other actions when they ask): gb_drama {action: "reply", text}. Freezone (canvas): node_gen {id, type, inputs} = fill that node using the wired input nodes (get → freezone.nodes): script → gb_drama {action: "node", id, text}; ai_image / video / audio → make it on Higgsfield and gb_drama {action: "node", id, prompt?, url}. You may add nodes: gb_drama {action: "node", type, title, text, from: id}. node_compose {id, inputs} = gb_drama {action: "node_compose", id} (the MCP joins the wired video nodes with ffmpeg and puts the MP4 in the node). merge mixes each beat's voice-over and the episode music when compose.voice / compose.music are on, and adds the subtitles (compose.subs) as a subtitle track + .srt file. media_out {what: style|char|scene|prop|still|clip|voice|music|node, name?, ep?, beat?, id?} saves any stored media as a file you can look at. If Higgsfield is not reachable, say so with gb_say and wait; the user can also upload pictures / clips on the page themselves. Actions: open | get | script {script, ep?} | beats {ep, seg, beats} | prompts {ep, beat, img_prompt, prompt} | still {ep, beat, url | path} | char {name, new_name?, role?, look?, url | path} | beat {ep, beat, status} | clip {ep, beat, url | path, sec?} | episode {ep, title?, hook?, summary?} | merge {ep} | clip_out {ep, beat} | asset {kind, name, look?, new_name?, url | path} | voice {name | ep+beat, url | path, desc?} | music {ep, url | path} | style {name?, prompt?} | node {id? , type?, title?, text?, prompt?, from?, url | path} | reply {text} | media_out {what, name?, ep?, beat?, id?} | srt {ep} | say {text} | done {id, note?}. ep / beat are 0-based.

url.description: char / clip: link to the picture / video (Higgsfield result src or download link)

name: gb_say
description: Post a message in the user's Greenbox side chat (the "🔌 Claude / Codex" panel next to the 3D view): say what you are doing, what you found, or ask a question. Use it for anything the user should read while looking at Greenbox; their answers come back through gb_inbox. Markdown is shown as plain text.

name: gb_inbox
description: Read what the user typed to you in the Greenbox side chat since the last read (they are cleared once read). wait = seconds to wait for a new message when there is none yet (0-50, default 0). Returns "(no new messages)" when empty.

wait.description: seconds to wait for a message (0-50)
